summary: Tenga Rinpoche (1932–2012) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Benchen Monastery. He served as Dorje Lopön at Rumtek Monastery (~1967–1984) and founded Benchen Monastery in 1976.

Tensei Kitabatake (1928–2024) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1950–1955). He later served at Ryukoku University as professor and president (1995–1999), and served as president of Gifu Shotoku Gakuen University (1999–2005).
Tenshin Tanouye (1938–2003) worked in Buddhist studies. He studied under and succeeded Sogen Omori, and he founded Chozen-ji.

Tenzin Dorjee is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Geshe Sonam Rinchen, Geshe Lobsang Tsephel, and Geshe Dawa. He served as translator at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives and General Secretary at Pullahari Monastery (attested 2000).

Tenzin Namdak (1927–2025) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under sGangs ru Tshul khrims rgyal mtshan, Lobpön Tsultrim Gyaltsen, and Shes rab bstan 'dzin rgyal mtshan, earned a degree at Menri Monastery, and founded Triten Norbutse Monastery.

Tenzin Norbu is a scholar in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He held a post at Columbia University and served as assistant professor and department head at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2026).

Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche is a scholar of religious studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics and Menri Monastery under teachers including Sangye Tenzin and Tenzin Namdak, he founded Ligmincha International and served at Menri and Rice University.

Ter Ellingson (born 1944) works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Concordia College, the University of Chicago, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison, and served as professor of music at the University of Washington from 1981 to 2016.

Terese Tse Bartholomew is a scholar in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and sinology. She earned an M.A. at the University of California, Los Angeles, and served as Curator of Himalayan Art and Chinese Decorative Art at the Asian Art Museum (attested 2001–2003).

Terry Kleeman (born 1955) is a scholar in sinology and religious studies. He studied at the University of British Columbia and was appointed professor at the University of Colorado Boulder around 1998.
Tertön Sogyal studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and he taught the 13th Dalai Lama.

Teruji Ishizu (1903–1972) was a scholar in religious studies and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo. His career included posts at Tohoku University, where he was president (1963–1966), and serving as president of Miyagi University of Education (1965).

Tessa J. Bartholomeusz (1958–2001) was a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Virginia, University of Florida, and Florida State University. She held posts at Virginia, IUPUI, and became Professor of Religion at Florida State in 1993.
Tessa Verney Wheeler (1893–1936) was a scholar in history and archaeology. She completed her studies at Addey and Stanhope School from 1905 to 1911 and at University College London from 1911 to 1914.

Tetsuei Sato (1902–1982) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1925–1931). He held professorships at Taisho University and Gifu Kyoritsu University (~1972), and was an emeritus professor at Ryukoku University (~1972–1982).
Tetsuhiko Shibata is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied at Taisho University under teachers Eijun Hattori, Yukan Ozawa, and Mitsuo Sato.

Tetsujiro Inoue (1856–1944) was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who studied at the University of Tokyo and Heidelberg, Leipzig, and Berlin universities. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo and second president of Daito Bunka University (1925).

Tetsuo Otani (born 1939) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda and Komazawa universities. He served as president of Komazawa University (2002–2006) and Tohoku Fukushi University (2015–2019), and as board chair of Tsuru University (2013–2016).

Tetsuro Noguchi (1932–2022) was a scholar in sinology, history and archaeology, and religious studies. During his academic career, he held posts at Yokohama National University, the University of Tsukuba, and J. F. Oberlin University.

Tetsuro Watsuji (1889–1960) was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo, Kyoto University, and under Martin Heidegger, holding ethics professorships at Kyoto University (1925–1949) and the University of Tokyo (1934–1949).
